pages.computers:
usage: wsp computers
  your computers: this Mac, each box you added and each cloud account, with what
  each has, whether it is connected, how many machines it holds and what runs
  there against its cap, and what each cloud spent today

  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell
pages.computers set:
usage: wsp computers set <computer> [--name <new>] [--ssh <login>]
       [--threads <n>] [--machines <n>] [--spend <usd>] [--size <cpu>x<memGb>]
       [--delete-after <minutes>] [--nap <minutes>|off]
       [--turn-limit <hours>|off] [--max-machines <n>] [--max-depth <n>]
       [--recipe <name>|none] [--reset <setting>]...
  what you set on one of your computers: its name, the ssh login it is reached
  by, how many threads run there at once, how long a quiet machine there runs
  before it naps, how long one turn there may run, the caps on agents starting
  agents, the recipe it follows, and on a cloud how many machines at once, how
  much it spends a day, the size a sub-thread's machine gets and how long a
  finished one stays; --reset takes a setting back to its default

  --name            what to call a computer you added from now, which every
                    listing then shows; its id, its projects and its machines
                    stay as they are
  --ssh             the login user@host the host reaches a computer you added by
                    over ssh from now, saved only once the computer it reaches
                    reads as that same one
  --threads         how many threads may run on that computer at once; a new one
                    waits past it
  --machines        how many machines may run on that cloud at once
  --spend           the dollars a day that cloud may spend before it starts no
                    new machine
  --size            on a cloud, the size a sub-thread's machine gets when the
                    thread starting it names none, as <cpu>x<memGb>; 2x4 until
                    it is set
  --delete-after    on a cloud, the minutes a finished sub-thread's machine
                    stays before it is deleted, 0 to 1440; 30 until it is set
  --nap             the minutes a quiet machine there runs before it naps, or
                    off
  --turn-limit      the hours one turn there may run before it is stopped, or
                    off; off on a computer you own and 6 on a cloud until it is
                    set
  --max-machines    how many machines may stand at once under one root thread;
                    defaults to 3
  --max-depth       how many levels of threads may stand under the root thread;
                    defaults to 2
  --recipe          the saved recipe it follows from now, by the name wsp
                    recipes shows, or none to keep what it has and follow
                    nothing
  --reset           a setting to take back to its default, by its flag's word;
                    repeats
  --json            print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line,
                    with everything else on stderr
  --state           the state file the host serves
  --host            run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp
                    hosts lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

       [--by agent|account|computer|project|model|source]

  agents logged outside wsp counted with wsp's threads as on the Usage page

  --by       how what was used is split: agent (the default), account, computer,

       [--reset <field>]...
  an agent's defaults on every computer: the model, effort and access a new
  thread on it starts on, and which models its picker lists

  --model         the model a new thread on it starts on, by the agent's own
                  slug
  --effort        the effort a new thread on it starts at, by the agent's own

  --access        how far a new thread on it may go without asking: ask,

  --hide          a model to take off its picker; a start still takes it by

  --show          a hidden model to put back on its picker; repeats
  --order         the models its picker lists first, comma separated; the rest
                  follow in the agent's own order
  --add-model     a model id the binary does not list, which a start may then
                  name; repeats
  --drop-model    a model id added before, taken back off; repeats
  --reset         put a field back on the agent's own: model, effort, access or

  --json          print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with

pages.agents setup:
usage: wsp agents setup <agent> [--on <computer>] [--enable | --disable]
       [--program <path>] [--config <folder>] [--arg <word>]...
       [--env <NAME>]... [--unset-env <NAME>]... [--reset <field>]...
  how an agent runs on one computer: on or off there, the program run in its
  place, its config folder, words added to every launch and variables every
  launch carries, each value typed where nothing echoes it

  --on           the computer, by the name wsp computers shows; this computer
                 without it
  --enable       offer the agent there again
  --disable      take the agent off that computer: the app's lists drop it there
                 and a start naming it is refused
  --program      the program run in the agent's place there, a path or a word on
                 its PATH
  --config       the folder there the agent keeps its config, sessions and
                 sign-in in, absolute and under that computer's home; sign it in
                 again there
  --arg          a word added to every turn's launch there; repeats, and
                 replaces any set before
  --env          a variable every launch there carries, by name, never one that
                 decides how the process starts (PATH, LD_*, NODE_OPTIONS and
                 the like); its value is asked for where nothing echoes it;
                 repeats
  --unset-env    a variable to take off its launch there, by name; repeats
  --reset        put a field back on the agent's own: program, config or args;
                 repeats
  --json         print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
                 everything else on stderr
  --state        the state file the host serves

                 hosts lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

pages.servers add:

       (--command "<line>" | --url <address> [--header <name>=<VARIABLE>]...)
       [--env <NAME>]... [--project [<name>]]
  writes one MCP server into an agent's own config: a command with its arguments
  and variables, or an address with its headers, each value read off this
  terminal's environment: the file names a variable and the value goes to the
  vault, an argument or the address naming a variable as ${NAME} keeps that name
  there, and an agent that reads no variable there refuses it

  --agent      the agent whose config takes the server, by its catalog id
  --on         the computer to read, by the name wsp computers shows; this
               computer without it, and a thread names its own
  --command    the line the server runs, its program and arguments in one quoted
               value, split as a shell splits it and nothing expanded; or --url
  --env        a variable the server is given, or one the address names as
               ${NAME}, by its name, its value read off the same name in this
               terminal's environment; an argument or the address may name it as
               ${NAME}; repeats
  --url        the server's https address; or --command
  --header     <name>=<VARIABLE>, a header sent to the address with its value
               read off that variable in this terminal's environment; repeats
  --project    put it in a project's file rather than the agent's own: alone
               with a thread, the thread's own project, or the project's name
               with --on
  --json       print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
               everything else on stderr

               hosts lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell
